Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.code

Class Compiler

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.code.Compiler
public final class Compiler extends Object
The Mandela compiler: a parsed statement list in, one CompiledFunction of bytecode out.

One pass, single traversal, no intermediate IR. The grammar is simple enough that each construct maps onto a fixed instruction shape, and skipping an IR keeps the whole tool chain — lexer, parser, compiler, machine — small enough to read in an afternoon, which is the point of a desktop scripting language.

The few things it does that are worth knowing before editing:

  • Top-level bindings are globals. A script's let is a global name, not a slot, so the REPL can build a session one statement at a time and an imported module's names stay reachable.
  • Tail expressions return. A function's last statement, when it is an expression, is the function's value. Statements therefore compile with a keepValue flag, and every construct guarantees the stack holds exactly one value when it says it does.
  • Captured locals are boxed eagerly. The first closure that reads a local marks its slot as holding a cell, and the already-emitted load/store instructions are rewritten (see CompiledFunction.Builder.boxSlot(int)). There is no close-upvalue pass and no scope exit to run.
  • finally is duplicated, not threaded. The finalizer is emitted on each path that leaves the try — normal end, caught error, filter mismatch, and every return / break / continue written inside it — so it runs exactly once per path without a JSR or a second handler stack.
  • Classes compile to a constructor. Field initialisers, init blocks and the extends call are sequenced into one synthesised init body whose slot 0 is this, which is what the machine calls after it allocates the instance.
  • Inside a class, a bare name may be a field or a method. The compiler knows the enclosing declaration's field and method names, so count += 1 and redraw() lower to this member operations at compile time. Nothing is resolved by name at run time, so there is no hidden-lookup tax and no ambiguity with globals.

Errors are thrown as LangException carrying the offending node's position, so mandela check and the editor's Problems panel get the same coordinates the parser reports.
